explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM judgments against human evaluations using correlation analysis on the same set of 97 stories, reporting Spearman correlations for each PDS component across multiple LLM models

prompts.notes: Appendix A.7 shows the five persona prompts used for Mixture-of-Personas prompting, tailored to each PDS component (e.g., 'You are a helpful AI who specializes in evaluating the genuineness and believability of characters, dialogue, and scenarios in stories.')

guidelines.notes: Appendix A.5 shows tutorial instructions and annotation layout with clear rating scales for each component (1-5 Likert scale)

sample_size.notes: Used stratified sampling method to create dataset of 97 stories (balanced across prompts, authorship, generation strategies) that both LLM and human evaluators assessed

quantitative_scores.notes: Average correlation across all components with Mixture-of-Personas prompting
Highest observed correlation across all components and models
Improved from 0.0786 with vanilla prompting (304% increase)

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Correlations range from 0.51-0.68 depending on component and model

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM judgments show moderate to strong correlations with human evaluations (Spearman ρ=0.51-0.68), with Mixture-of-Personas prompting improving correlation by 20.43% on average. No single LLM excels across all components, suggesting component-specific model selection is optimal.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluators assessed identical PDS components on the 1-5 Likert scale. Only human evaluators assessed authorship likelihood (human vs LLM).
